seo.h1: M-210 Titanium Dioxide for Masterbatch and Plastics Evaluation

hero.summaryLead: A chloride-process rutile titanium dioxide pigment with inorganic and organic treatment, documented for polyolefin masterbatch, PE/PP/ABS engineering plastics, and PS/copolymer applications.
hero.summaryBody: The current profile identifies hiding and tinting strength, dispersibility, dry-powder fluidity, processing behavior and bluish-undertone direction as evaluation priorities. Review the typical data and confirm suitability in your own polymer, formulation, processing and end-use conditions.

positioning.heading: Where M-210 Fits in Product Evaluation
positioning.lead: M-210 is a chloride-process rutile titanium dioxide pigment specially treated with inorganic and organic compounds for masterbatch and plastics evaluation.
positioning.body: Use M-210 as a candidate when hiding, tinting, dispersibility, powder handling and processing behavior are relevant. Final selection should account for polymer, carrier resin, additives, pigment loading, processing temperature, equipment, appearance and destination documents.
decisionPoints: PE, PP and ABS engineering-plastics direction
Evaluation of color direction, hiding and tinting, dispersion, fluidity and processing

applications.heading: Plastics and Masterbatch Directions to Evaluate
applications.intro: Review each documented direction in your own polymer system, processing and end-use conditions.

items.title: Polyolefin Masterbatch
items.body: Evaluate M-210 at the intended pigment loading and carrier resin. Confirm dispersion, hiding and tinting, color direction, powder handling, processing and dilution performance.

items.title: Engineering Plastics: PE, PP and ABS
items.body: Test M-210 in the actual PE, PP or ABS formulation, additives, temperature and equipment. Confirm dispersion, appearance, processing behavior and end-use suitability.

items.title: PS and Its Copolymers
items.body: Review M-210 in the intended PS or copolymer system. Confirm compatibility, color, hiding and tinting, dispersion and processing under actual conditions.

evaluation.heading: What to Evaluate in Your Plastics Formulation
evaluation.intro: Use the documented M-210 profile and typical data to frame buyer testing.

groups.heading: Optical and Dispersion Review
items: Bluish-undertone direction in the complete formulation
Hiding power and tinting strength at intended loading
Dispersion in the selected polymer and carrier system

groups.heading: Processing and Qualification Review
items: Dry-powder fluidity in handling and feeding conditions
Processing behavior at actual temperature and equipment settings
Compatibility with resin and additive package
Application conditions, destination needs and sample-validation results

evaluation.disclaimer: These evaluation priorities identify what to check during buyer testing. They do not guarantee fixed results.
